lawyer:
HN Nandi, Advocate -For the Petitioner
Md Nurul Amin with Mizanur Rahman, Advocates -For the Opposite Party
parties:
Majida Khatoon ------ Petitioner
vs.
Md Mominul Huq and ors ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Pre-emptor petitioner obtained this Rule against the judgment and order dated 22-8-94 of the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Jhenaidah in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 16 of 1994 affirming that dated 31-5-94 of the learned Assistant Judge, Kaliganj Jhenaidah in Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 1994. 

 2. Pre-emptor instituted the case under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act for pre-emption of the case land claiming as co-sharer. The case of the pre-emptor is that she is a co-sharer by purchase of the case holding, opposite party No. 2 transferred the case land in favour of opposite party No. 1 at a consideration of Taka 5,000 but with a view to defeat the right of pre-emption, the deed was executed mentioning as exchange deed showing exchange of the case land with the land of opposite party No.1 measuring 8 acres of agricultural land situated far away and the case land is situated within the Kaliganj Municipality. It is the further case of the pre-emptor that the transaction in question is not a deed of exchange but it was an out-and-out sale. The alleged exchange deed was executed on 28-7-93 but the pre-emptor had no knowledge about the said transaction which he came to know on 29-1-94 after taking certified copy of the deed. It is the further case of the pre-emptor that no delivery of possession of the land was given to the opposite party No. 2 which has been allegedly exchanged as described in schedule 2 to the pre-emption petition. 

 3. Purchaser opposite party No.1 contested the case by filing a written objection denying all material allegations made in the pre-emption petition. His case is that the case is barred by limitation and the transaction in question is a deed of exchange. His further case is that he was the owner of schedule 2 land as described in the pre-emption petition and the opposite party No. 2 was the owner of the case land which has been described in the schedule 1 to the pre-emption petition. Opposite Party No. 2 offered for exchange of the case land with his land and upon consultation, both the parties have executed the exchange deed on 28-7-93. The further case of the purchaser is that after the execution of the exchange deed, he went into possession of the case land and opposite party No. 2 got possession of schedule 2 land and therefore, the case is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The learned Assistant Judge upon consideration of the evidence on record by judgment and order dated 31-5-94 dismissed the pre-emption case. Pre-emptor being aggrieved by the said judgment and order preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 16 of 1994 which was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Jhenaidah who by his judgment and order dated 22-8-94 dismissed the appeal and affirmed that of the learned Assistant Judge. 

 5. Mr HN Nandi, learned Advocate appearing for the preemptor petitioner, submits that the courts below upon a total non consideration of the material evidence on record held that the transaction in question is an exchange deed and not an out and out sale. Mr Nandi further submits that the court of appeal upon a superficial consideration of the evidence on record disbelieved the date of knowledge of the pre-emptor and thereby has committed an error of law in holding that the case is barred by limitation. Mr Nurul Amin, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the purchaser opposite party No. 1, on the other hand, submits that both the courts below concurrently found that the transaction in question is not an out and out sale but a deed of exchange, these findings being the findings of fact, this court in exercising revisional jurisdiction cannot disturb those findings of fact. The learned Advocate further submits that the courts below upon proper appreciation of the evidence on record have come to the definite finding that the pre-emptor has failed to prove that she came to know about the alleged transaction on 29-1-94 and dismissed the case on the ground of limitation, this finding of fact cannot be disturbed by this court in the absence of any misreading or non consideration of the evidence on record. 

 6. The disputed instrument in question, Ext. 2(ga), has been described as ewaj ie deed of exchange. According to the pre-emptor, the transaction is an out and out sale and not a deed of exchange. The purchaser opposite party No.1 claims that it was a deed of exchange and therefore, the pre emptor is not entitled to preempt the case land under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act. In support of his case, the pre-emptor petitioner has examined 3 witnesses and the purchaser opposite party No.1 has examined 2 witnesses. Of them, OPW 1 is the purchaser and OPW 2 is the son of Kalipada who allegedly exchanged the case land with the purchaser. 

 7. Admittedly, the case land is a barren land. According to the pre-emptor, after the execution of the alleged deed of exchange, the purchaser did not take possession of the case land in order to defeat the right of pre-emption and on 29-1-94 the purchaser went to the case land with a surveyor for measurement of the case land when on query to him, he disclosed that he has exchanged the case land. Thereafter, he filed the case on 23-2-94 within 4 months from the date of knowledge. 

 8. Before the trial Court, the purchaser raised two preliminary objections ie the pre-emptor is not a cosharer and that the application under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act is not maintainable. These two issues were however found in favour of the pre-emptor. Only dispute between the parties is whether the transaction in question is an out and out sale or not and whether the case is barred by limitation. The trial Court upon consideration of the evidence on record came to the conclusion that the transaction in question is not an out and out sale but a deed of exchange and therefore, the pre-emptor is not entitled to preempt the case land under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act. The court of appeal below affirmed the said finding. The court of appeal below upon consideration of the evidence of OPWs 1 and 2 held that the claim of the pre-emptor that even after the execution of the deed of exchange, the opposite party No. 2 did not get possession of schedule No. 2 land and that the purchaser is in possession of the case land has not been established by adducing reliable evidence. According to Mr Nandi, this finding of the learned Subordinate Judge is based upon non consideration of material evidence of PW 1 and PW 3. Mr Nandi drew my attention to the statement of PW 1 who states even after exchange, opposite party No. 2 did not possess schedule 2 land which statement has not been challenged by the purchaser in course of cross examination. Mr Nandi also referred to a statement of PW 3 who states that Afsar and Moksed, the brothers of opposite party No.1, have been possessing the schedule 2 land which statement has not been challenged by the purchaser opposite party No. 1. Mr Nurul Amin the learned Advocate submits that OPWs 1 and 2 in their evidence specifically state that opposite party No. 2 was given possession of the schedule 2 land after the execution of the deed of exchange and that he is in possession by cultivating Boro paddy, I have perused the statement of OPWs 1 and 2 who state that the opposite party No. 2 got possession of the schedule 2 land after execution of the deed of exchange and that he has been cultivating the said land. 

 9. The court of appeal below has discussed the evidence on record elaborately and after appreciating, the evidence disbelieved the plea of the pre-emptor that opposite party No. 2 did not get possession of the schedule 2 land after execution of the alleged deed of exchange. This finding is based upon consideration of the evidence on record and the learned Advocate for the petitioner has failed to point out that this finding is based upon non-consideration of material evidence on record or of misreading evidence on record. Mr Nandi though pointed out that the evidence of PWs 1 and 3 in this regard has not been controverted by cross examining them but I find that OPWs in their statements made positive assertion disputing the statements of PWs 1 and 3. Therefore, it cannot be said that the finding was not based upon non consideration of the evidence on record, rather 1 find that this finding is based upon overall consideration of the evidence on record. Considering all these aspects of the matter, I am of the view that the transaction in question is not an out and out sale but a deed of exchange and therefore, the pre-emptor is not entitled to preempt the case land under section 2 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act. The court below have given due consideration of the evidence on record and they have rightly arrived at a finding that the transaction is a deed of exchange. This finding being a finding of fact cannot be disturbed in exercise of revisional jurisdiction. 

 10. As regards the finding as to limitation, I am of the view that the findings of the courts below that the case is barred by limitation are mere hypothesis without consideration of the material evidence on record. Admittedly, the case land is a barren land and admittedly no notice was served upon the pre-emptor who is a co-sharer in the case holding. His positive assertion is that he came to know about the said transaction on 29-1-94 when the purchaser went to the case land for measurement. PW 2 Mostafizur Rahman corroborated him in this regard. The deed in question was registered on 28-7-93. The pre emptor claims that she came to know on 29-1-94 and the case was filed on 23-2-94. As mentioned above, no notice for sale/exchange was served upon the preemptor and the purchaser did not mention as to his act of possession in the case immediately after the registration of the deed. Admittedly the case land is barren land and therefore, the reason for disbelieving that as there is no statement in the pre-emption petition about the measurement of the case land and that there is also no statement about the presence of opposite party No. 2 at the time of measurement, his claim cannot be believed, are mere hypothesis and not based upon consideration of material evidence on record.
